title: CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
creator: David J. Malan / Harvard CS50
prerequisites: No prior programming required; ordinary computer use.
access: Free OpenCourseWare; submission services and optional certificates have separate account or enrollment arrangements.
why: A structured first programming course whose sequence includes exceptions, tests, and files, all immediately useful in a sensor logger.
first_task: Complete functions and conditionals, then implement and test a counts-to-millimetres function against three reference values.
limitations: Requires sustained exercise work; it is not embedded firmware or real-time control training.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official beginner audience statement, ten-topic syllabus, and browser/local-computer learning options. Recommendation reflects syllabus review, not personal course completion.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, Third Edition
creator: Al Sweigart
prerequisites: No programming background; willingness to edit and run small scripts.
access: Author-hosted book free to read online; print and other editions available commercially. Separate video course does not mirror the current edition exactly.
why: File and table tasks give a new programmer useful bench-work outcomes before larger software architecture becomes necessary.
first_task: Read debugging and file I/O, then organize copied experiment logs by a stable naming convention while preserving originals.
limitations: Automation libraries and external services change; verify current APIs and practice file-changing tasks on disposable copies.
evidence_note: Reviewed the author's third-edition description, free-reading statement, and contents including debugging, files, CSV/JSON, and command-line programs.

title: Pro Git, Second Edition
creator: Scott Chacon and Ben Straub
prerequisites: Basic files and terminal use; no hosted repository required for the opening exercises.
access: Complete book available free on the official Git site; print editions sold separately.
why: Explains the local snapshot model before advanced collaboration, helping a maker preserve small, understandable design decisions.
first_task: In a disposable folder, commit a calibration file, change one value, inspect the diff, and restore the earlier version.
limitations: Text diffs explain code well but do not provide semantic CAD comparisons or a complete backup policy.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official full-book contents, author attribution, edition, and online access.

title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
creator: MIT Missing Semester teaching team
prerequisites: Some coding experience; comfort practicing in a terminal.
access: Public course notes and linked lectures; no claim of live MIT enrollment or credit.
why: Addresses the tools around programming that make repeated experiments easier to reproduce and diagnose.
first_task: Use the shell and Git lessons to search a copied log directory and preserve one small, tested logger change.
limitations: Command-line conventions and tooling differ by platform; exercises complement rather than replace learning a language.
evidence_note: Reviewed the 2026 syllabus covering shell, environments, debugging, Git, shipping code, agentic coding, and code quality.

title: The Python Tutorial
creator: Python documentation contributors
level: beginner to Python after basic programming
prerequisites: Understand variables, loops, and functions; the official tutorial explicitly assumes some programming background.
why: A reliable reference for exact language behavior after a guided course supplies the first mental model.
first_task: Read numbers, input/output, and exceptions while tracing the sensor logger's text-to-number conversion.
limitations: Not designed as a first-ever programming course; select the documentation matching the installed Python version.
evidence_note: Reviewed the tutorial's audience statement and contents, including numeric operations, modules, I/O, and exceptions.

title: Understanding PID Control
creator: MathWorks
prerequisites: Algebra and the idea of reference minus measurement; simulation experience helps.
access: Public video series; MATLAB/Simulink software access is separate and is not required for the handbook's Python lab.
why: The separate saturation and noise episodes make practical failure mechanisms visible before deeper control mathematics.
first_task: Watch the introductory and anti-windup episodes, then predict the two integral traces in control_lab.py.
limitations: Product demonstrations are not a universal tuning recipe; a real plant still needs identified limits and dynamics.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official series list including PID introduction, anti-windup, derivative noise, tuning, and models.

title: Modern Robotics companion video lessons
creator: Kevin Lynch / Northwestern University
level: intermediate; selected introductory lessons approachable earlier
prerequisites: Trigonometry for initial geometry; linear algebra and calculus for the full sequence.
access: Public companion videos; associated book, software, and course enrollment have separate links and arrangements.
why: Connects frames and configuration to kinematics and dynamics in a coherent technical progression.
first_task: Watch configuration-space and planar rigid-motion lessons, then draw the two frames in the handbook's camera example.
limitations: The full material is mathematically demanding and does not teach beginner fabrication or certify a robot mechanism.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official chapter-organized video index, including configuration, transforms, forward/inverse kinematics, dynamics, and control.

title: ROS 2 Jazzy tutorials
creator: ROS 2 documentation contributors / Open Robotics community
prerequisites: Python or C++, command-line use, and a compatible ROS 2 environment; the chosen binary route is Ubuntu 24.04.
access: Free official documentation and open-source tooling; computer/VM resources are separate.
why: A staged path for coordinating several robot components after their individual geometry and behavior are understood.
first_task: Complete beginner command-line tutorials and inspect a publisher/subscriber pair before publishing simulated joint states.
limitations: Jazzy is a supported deliberate choice, not the newest release. Mac native source builds, virtualization, USB, and graphics require separate setup verification.
evidence_note: Reviewed official repository source because the rendered site denied automated access; also checked Installation.rst for Ubuntu 24.04 and rolling Releases.rst for Jazzy support through May 2029 and Lyrical through May 2031.

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python
creator: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, and Jonathan Taylor
prerequisites: Algebra, introductory probability/statistics, and basic Python; deeper sections benefit from mathematical maturity.
access: Author-hosted PDF download free; print edition sold separately.
why: Develops model comparison and assessment, helping readers distinguish fitting examples from useful generalization.
first_task: Read classification and resampling material, then explain why a session-level split changes the vision experiment's evaluation.
limitations: Broader and more mathematical than a first image-processing recipe; Python lab dependencies need a compatible environment.
evidence_note: Reviewed the authors' page confirming the 2023 Python edition, downloadable PDF, chapter topics, and labs.

title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
creator: fast.ai
prerequisites: Some coding experience, preferably Python; comfort running notebooks and installing dependencies.
access: Free course materials; GPU or hosted notebook compute may involve separate limits or charges.
why: An applied route from training to deployment once a reader can establish a baseline and an honest evaluation split.
first_task: Work through an image-classification lesson, then evaluate new-session photographs against the handbook's threshold baseline.
limitations: Not an introduction to programming or a guarantee that every historical notebook works unchanged with current libraries.
evidence_note: Reviewed official audience guidance and Part 1 lessons covering deployment, neural networks, NLP, trees, and CNNs.

title: CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python
creator: Brian Yu and David J. Malan / Harvard CS50
prerequisites: Official prerequisite: CS50x or at least one year of Python experience.
access: Free OpenCourseWare; project feedback requires the stated account workflow, and optional certificates/enrollment are separate.
why: Places learning alongside search, knowledge, and uncertainty, giving a broader foundation than calling an LLM API.
first_task: Complete the search lesson and explain the state, actions, and goal test of a small simulated positioning problem.
limitations: The word introduction refers to AI, not first-time programming; physical control and hardware safety are outside its scope.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official seven-topic syllabus, explicit prerequisite, projects, and free OpenCourseWare participation description.

title: OpenCV tutorials
creator: OpenCV contributors
level: beginner after Python; intermediate for calibration
prerequisites: Python or C++ basics and array concepts; linear algebra helps with camera geometry.
access: Free official documentation and open-source library.
why: Provides inspectable classical vision operations before a project needs a learned model.
first_task: Threshold a fixed image region, compare changing illumination, then read calibration before converting pixels into millimetres.
limitations: Camera setup, distortion, and measurement uncertainty remain the builder's responsibility; select documentation matching the installed version.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official tutorial index and camera-calibration lesson; the 4.x URL resolved to 4.13.0 during review.

title: Eclipse Mosquitto documentation
creator: Eclipse Mosquitto project
prerequisites: Basic networking and command-line use; complete the in-memory message lab first.
access: Free documentation and open-source broker/client tools.
why: An implementation reference for moving a tested messaging policy onto a local broker with visible logs.
first_task: Run a local-only publish/subscribe exercise, then configure authentication and topic permissions before allowing wider access.
limitations: Broker installation and secure operation are separate responsibilities; a working message exchange is not a safe actuator interface.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official links for broker/client man pages, configuration, authentication, dynamic security, TLS, and MQTT features.

title: MQTT Version 5.0 specification
creator: OASIS MQTT Technical Committee
prerequisites: A completed publish/subscribe exercise and familiarity with message delivery terminology.
why: The authoritative place to resolve delivery and retained-message semantics when an implementation assumption matters.
first_task: Find QoS 1 behavior and explain why the application's command identifiers are still necessary.
limitations: Dense reference, not a beginner course or proof of exactly-once physical actuation.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official March 2019 standard's introduction and delivery descriptions.

title: IoT Device Cybersecurity Capability Core Baseline (NISTIR 8259A)
creator: Michael Fagan, Katerina Megas, Karen Scarfone, and Matthew Smith / NIST
prerequisites: Understand the device's users, interfaces, stored data, and update path; no cryptography implementation required.
why: Turns broad security intentions into device capabilities that can be reviewed during an early design.
first_task: Document device identity, permitted interfaces, update/recovery behavior, and the logs needed to recognize a fault.
limitations: A baseline for requirements, not a build recipe, certification, or complete threat model for every deployment.
evidence_note: Reviewed the official publication page and May 2020 PDF identifying the device cybersecurity capability baseline.

title: I2C-bus specification and user manual (UM10204)
creator: NXP Semiconductors
prerequisites: Digital voltage levels, pull-up resistors, and basic clock/data timing.
why: Explains why a shared sensor bus has electrical limits as well as addresses and software calls.
first_task: Draw SDA and SCL with their pull-ups, identify each device's address and voltage limits, then inspect the applicable timing mode.
limitations: Read together with the actual controller and sensor data sheets; it is not permission to use arbitrary wire lengths or pull-up values.
evidence_note: Reviewed revision 7.0, dated October 1, 2021, including bus overview, terminology, addressing, and electrical/timing scope.
